The function \(f\) is odd, so \(f(-x) = -f(x)\). The function \(g\) is even, so \(g(-x) = g(x)\). We evaluate the parity of the composition from the inside out:

- \(f(x)\) is odd (odd function applied to the identity \(x\)).
- \(g(f(x))\): \(g\) is even, and \(g\) of any function is even because \(g(-u(x)) = g(u(x))\). So this is even.
- \(f(g(f(x)))\): \(f\) applied to an even function is even, because \(f(u(-x)) = f(u(x))\).
- \(g(f(g(f(x))))\): \(g\) of an even function is even.
- \(f(g(f(g(f(x)))))\): \(f\) of an even function is even.
- \(f(f(g(f(g(f(x))))))\): \(f\) of an even function is even.

Thus the entire composition is even.

Answer: even
